objectives.text: Keep the canal Panamanian, neutral and open to all flags. The 1977 Torrijos-Carter treaties handed the waterway to Panama; in 2025 Trump spoke of 'taking back' the canal, and President Mulino answered that Panama would keep ownership. The objective is to hold that line without a fight, which is why the concession went to security rather than to sovereignty.

objectives.text: Keep the port concessions under Panamanian law and the revenue at home. A Panamanian lawsuit sought to annul the 25-year CK Hutchison contract for the ports at both canal entrances as unconstitutional, while the BlackRock purchase was pushed through as the solution Washington praised.

means.text: Security for sovereignty, traded. The April 2025 memorandum with the US Defence Department reopens a rotational US presence at three former bases along the canal and records a declaration on first and free transit for US warships. The price was a US military presence that Panama's own treaty history had ended.

means.text: Port review as leverage. Mulino agreed to review Chinese-linked businesses in Panama, including the CK Hutchison ports, after Rubio's February 2025 ultimatum; the review is a regulatory lever that Panama can turn on and off.

constraints.text: Street and social cost. An indefinite strike from 28 April 2025 against pension reform and US interference paralysed Bocas del Toro; Chiquita lost more than US$75 million and fired thousands of its roughly 6,500 Panamanian workers; Panama declared a state of emergency in June 2025 after deadly clashes. The government cannot make a US-facing move without a domestic price.

constraints.text: Opposition to the US pact. The opposition calls the security memorandum a 'camouflaged invasion', and the protests named the deal among their grievances. The alignment Mulino needs for the canal is the one his own politics resist.

paradoxes.text: The treaties that gave the canal back in 1977 barred the foreign bases that the 2025 memorandum brings back along the waterway. Panama defends its sovereignty over the canal with the presence that sovereignty was meant to end, and the protests show the cost is paid at home.

grand_strategy.reading: Panama's strategy is to keep the canal Panamanian and its revenue flowing, and in 2025 the only protector of both was the power that had threatened to take the canal back. Mulino paid for US cover with a military presence and a rupture with Beijing's Belt and Road, and kept the Chinese-linked ports under review rather than seized. The cost shows at home in the strike, the emergency and the word 'invasion', so the next test is whether neutrality of the canal survives a patron that is also its loudest claimant.

stances.note: Cooperates out of necessity, resists alignment. The canal 'taking back' line (Trump, from January 2025), the April 2025 memorandum reopening a rotational US presence along the canal, and Mulino's sitting at the Shield of the Americas (March 2026). Reluctant_partner is our reading, not a source's word: the sources record the cooperation and the opposition's 'camouflaged invasion' charge. Trend warming since Mulino declared the crisis with Washington over (2 January 2026). Bond grievance, in the opposition's telling and in the protests; the USA card reads the bond as none. Confidence C for that reason.

stances.note: Transactional, and cooling. Panama signed the Belt and Road memorandum in 2017 and in February 2025 instructed its embassy in Beijing to give the 90-day notice of withdrawal, after Rubio's ultimatum on Chinese influence over the canal. The CK Hutchison ports were put under review and a Panamanian lawsuit sought to annul the 25-year contract as unconstitutional. Partner, not reluctant partner: no source calls the Panama-China relation reluctant. Trend cooling is our reading from the withdrawal; Beijing called the pressure coercion. Bond none: no kinship and no open grievance from Panama's side. Confidence C: press reporting only, no Chinese or Panamanian government text read.

stances.note: Panama suspended diplomatic relations on 29 July 2024, the day after Venezuela's presidential vote that the opposition said Maduro had lost, and pulled its diplomats out of Caracas; Mulino said that silence would make Panama complicit. Rival is our reading: the suspension is the only hostile act sourced, and no source calls the relation a rivalry. Trend warming: consular services were restored in June 2025, and Wikipedia records the reopening of Venezuela's embassy in Panama City in October 2025, not confirmed by a second source. Bond grievance: the disputed election is the wound. The January 2026 seizure of Maduro (USA card) is not read from the Panamanian side and is left to the next pass.

stances_toward.note: Partner, warming, confidence C. Mulino's campaign promise to close the Darién jungle crossing is unresolved (analysts called it unviable, VOA, 2024); nothing found says de la Espriella has taken a position. stances_toward.note: From 'taking back' the canal (Jan 2025) to a partner that complied: Rubio's ultimatum on Chinese influence (2 Feb 2025), Panama's exit from the Belt and Road, the BlackRock purchase of CK Hutchison's Balboa and Cristobal ports praised by Trump as 'reclaiming' the canal (Mar 2025), the Hegseth memorandum of 9 Apr 2025 reopening a rotational US presence at three former bases and a declaration on 'first and free' transit for US warships; Mulino declared the crisis over on 2 Jan 2026 and sat at the Shield of the Americas (7 Mar 2026). Partner, not ally: no treaty, Panama refuses foreign bases, and the opposition calls the MOU a 'camouflaged invasion'. Warming. Bond - none. Panama has no card yet.
